name: Ca nien
summary: Cá niên is the mountain-stream fish. Vietnam Airlines places it in Sơn Hà, Trà Bồng, and Tây Trà, and spells the rainy season as lunar April to August. ZaloPay places it in Trà Bồng and Ba Tơ. The provincial introduction spells cá niêng and does not describe a plate.
taste: Vietnam Airlines calls the meat white, sweet, firm, not fishy, and low in bones. ZaloPay calls it firm, fragrant, and not fishy.
howToEat: Vietnam Airlines: the usual plate is the whole fish, gut included, grilled with salt and chili, or grilled over an open flame. Also a turmeric braise, fried crisp, or a sour soup with lá giang. The rainy season it prints is lunar months 4 through 8, when the meat is fattest.
ZaloPay: grill until the skin colors, and dip in hand-pounded chili salt with lime. It says the fish is a rainy-season catch, not a year-round one, in Trà Bồng and Ba Tơ.
The provincial introduction on the Trương Quang Trọng ward site names cá niêng in the mountains and prints no method.
No hour was printed. The hour is Check on arrival.
where: Sơn Hà, Trà Bồng, and Tây Trà on Vietnam Airlines. Trà Bồng and Ba Tơ on ZaloPay. Not the city center.
priceBand: Vietnam Airlines prints 300,000–800,000, and the currency word on that line is VDN, a kilogram, fresh or frozen. ZaloPay printed no price.
seoDescription: Cá niên from the mountain streams. Vietnam Airlines prints 300,000–800,000 VDN a kilogram. ZaloPay adds Ba Tơ and a chili-salt dip. The hour is Check on arrival.
